name: girvan_newman
author: c7c2ef65
description: Finds communities (groups of nodes more connected to each other than to the rest) by the Girvan-Newman method: repeatedly removes the edge with the highest betweenness, the bridge most shortest paths cross, until the graph splits. Use it for questions like 'what natural groups exist', 'how does the network break apart', or 'split the club into two factions' (num_communities=2). By default it returns the split with the highest modularity; set num_communities for a fixed number of groups. Works on small and medium graphs (up to about 200 nodes and 1,500 edges, e.g. karate, lesmis, projects, courses or a filtered subgraph); larger graphs return an error. Treats every graph as undirected and unweighted. Returns {num_communities, modularity, edges_removed, communities}: each community has its size, a graph_id of its subgraph for further tools, and its members (id, label), most connected first. result_graph_id is the largest community.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

num_communities.description: Number of communities to split into, from 1 to the number of nodes. Leave it out to get the split with the best modularity.

top_k.description: How many of the largest communities to list.
